partners.mechanism_chain: HSPB1 (HGNC:4907) —DISRUPTS→ Protein folding and quality control (GO:0006457); Protein folding and quality control (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000988); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000988) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuron degeneration (HP:0007175); PSMC3 (HGNC:9985) —DISRUPTS→ Ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process (GO:0006511); Ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process (GO:0006511) —LEADS_TO→ Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000988); Ubiquitin-proteasome system (GO:0000988) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental abnormality (HP:0011105). Loss-of-function mutations in HSPB1 disrupt protein folding and quality control, leading to downstream effects on the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), ultimately causing motor neuron degeneration. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PSMC3, a core component of the 26S proteasome, directly impair the ubiquitin-dependent protein catabolic process within the UPS, also leading to neurodevelopmental abnormalities. The convergence occurs at the ubiquitin-proteasome system, a critical cellular pathway for both diseases.
